### Domain 5: Selection of the reported result

**5.1 — No information.** The reported result is the ITT hazard ratio for the composite primary endpoint in all randomized participants (article, p. 6, lines 42–47; endpoint definition, p. 6, lines 72–76). The protocol contains an analysis plan for the primary endpoint: it specifies ITT, Kaplan–Meier/log-rank and Cox methods (protocol, p. 46, lines 20–32). The 2014 protocol version and its listed changes are documented (protocol, pp. 24, 45, lines 20–29), and the supplement identifies an original SAP as the only version (p. 2, lines 7–10). These are direct evidence of plan content and document chronology, but do not establish when investigators finalized or had access to unblinded outcome data. Nor do they fully resolve correspondence: the plan specifies Cox regression, while the reported primary-endpoint HR is identified as a Fine–Gray competing-risks analysis (article, p. 6, lines 100–104). The protocol also says analysis deviations would be described in the final report (p. 19, lines 25–31), but the supplied passages do not explain this method difference. Thus, neither timely prespecification nor result-driven change is established.

**5.2 — No information.** The protocol and article identify the composite primary endpoint and define operative and cardiovascular mortality (protocol, p. 28, lines 13–22; appendix, p. 5, lines 18–32; article, p. 3, lines 31–41). The article also reports secondary endpoints and subgroup analyses (article, p. 3, lines 36–39, 86–90). But the supplied evidence does not establish the complete set of eligible measurements within this outcome domain, or that this endpoint was selected over another eligible measurement because of its result. Lack of evidence of selection is not evidence that selection did not occur.

**5.3 — No information.** The protocol specifies ITT, time-to-first-event Kaplan–Meier/log-rank and Cox methods, and prespecified subgroup analyses (protocol, p. 46, lines 20–32); the article reports the primary endpoint using a Fine–Gray analysis (article, p. 6, lines 100–104). The materials also report Kaplan–Meier estimates and a per-protocol analysis (article, p. 3, lines 63–75, 90–95; appendix, p. 16, lines 15–22). These show multiple analyses, not that the reported analysis was chosen because it was favorable. The reason for the method difference and the complete eligible analysis set remain unknown.

**Resulting Domain 5 judgment: Some concerns.** The unresolved timing and method correspondence leave prespecification uncertain, and the supplied evidence does not establish whether the reported result was selected from alternatives on the basis of results. No direct evidence of results-driven selection is provided.
